name: Static shot
description: Locked-off frame — no camera movement at all.
prompt: locked-off static shot. Movement: hold one fixed camera position for the full clip. Speed: still and steady. Framing: keep the same angle, height, lens distance and composition. End: finish with the same framing and camera position.
prompt_template: {scene}. Camera: locked-off static shot. Movement: hold one fixed camera position for the full clip. Speed: still and steady. Framing: keep the same angle, height, lens distance and composition. End: finish with the same framing and camera position.
best_for: Dialogue holds, tableaux, and moments that need calm and control.
tips: Let the subject carry the motion: a gesture, breath, wind in hair or drifting smoke.
Say "the camera does not move" once more at the end of the prompt if the model keeps drifting.

name: Pan right
description: Horizontal rotation left-to-right from a fixed point.
prompt: pan right. Movement: rotate the camera horizontally from left to right from one fixed point. Speed: smooth constant rotation. Framing: keep the horizon level while new space enters from the right side of the frame. End: settle on a clear final composition.
prompt_template: {scene}. Camera: pan right. Movement: rotate the camera horizontally from left to right from one fixed point. Speed: smooth constant rotation. Framing: keep the horizon level while new space enters from the right side of the frame. End: settle on a clear final composition.
best_for: Revealing a landscape or handing off to a subject entering frame right.
tips: Start the frame with open space on the right so the pan has something to reveal.
Keep the pan under half a turn per clip; wide sweeps smear detail.

name: Pan left
description: Horizontal rotation right-to-left from a fixed point.
prompt: pan left. Movement: rotate the camera horizontally from right to left from one fixed point. Speed: smooth constant rotation. Framing: keep the horizon level while new space enters from the left side of the frame. End: settle on a clear final composition.
prompt_template: {scene}. Camera: pan left. Movement: rotate the camera horizontally from right to left from one fixed point. Speed: smooth constant rotation. Framing: keep the horizon level while new space enters from the left side of the frame. End: settle on a clear final composition.
best_for: Following a subject moving left or unveiling a reveal to frame left.
tips: Start the frame with open space on the left so the pan has something to reveal.
Keep the pan under half a turn per clip; wide sweeps smear detail.

name: Whip pan right
description: Fast snap rotation to the right with motion blur.
prompt: whip pan right. Movement: rotate rapidly from the starting direction toward a new target on the right. Speed: fast snap with brief motion blur during the rotation. Framing: begin on one readable composition and land on a second readable target. End: settle into a sharp final frame.
prompt_template: {scene}. Camera: whip pan right. Movement: rotate rapidly from the starting direction toward a new target on the right. Speed: fast snap with brief motion blur during the rotation. Framing: begin on one readable composition and land on a second readable target. End: settle into a sharp final frame.
best_for: Energetic scene transitions and connecting two beats with a blur cut.
tips: Name the landing target ("land on the open doorway on the right") so the clip ends on something readable.
Cut out of the blur, or chain the next clip from the settled last frame.

name: Whip pan left
description: Fast snap rotation to the left with motion blur.
prompt: whip pan left. Movement: rotate rapidly from the starting direction toward a new target on the left. Speed: fast snap with brief motion blur during the rotation. Framing: begin on one readable composition and land on a second readable target. End: settle into a sharp final frame.
prompt_template: {scene}. Camera: whip pan left. Movement: rotate rapidly from the starting direction toward a new target on the left. Speed: fast snap with brief motion blur during the rotation. Framing: begin on one readable composition and land on a second readable target. End: settle into a sharp final frame.
best_for: Energetic scene transitions and connecting two beats with a blur cut.
tips: Name the landing target ("land on the window on the left") so the clip ends on something readable.
Cut out of the blur, or chain the next clip from the settled last frame.

name: Tilt up
description: Vertical rotation upward from a fixed point.
prompt: tilt up. Movement: rotate the camera upward from one fixed point. Speed: smooth constant tilt. Framing: keep the vertical subject or architecture centered as the frame travels upward. End: land on the upper target.
prompt_template: {scene}. Camera: tilt up. Movement: rotate the camera upward from one fixed point. Speed: smooth constant tilt. Framing: keep the vertical subject or architecture centered as the frame travels upward. End: land on the upper target.
best_for: Reverent reveals — rising from feet to face, or up a tall structure.
tips: Frame the start on the base of the subject (feet, foundation, trunk) and name what the tilt lands on.
Tall vertical subjects read best; flat scenes give the tilt nothing to follow.

name: Tilt down
description: Vertical rotation downward from a fixed point.
prompt: tilt down. Movement: rotate the camera downward from one fixed point. Speed: smooth constant tilt. Framing: keep the vertical subject or architecture centered as the frame travels downward. End: land on the lower target.
prompt_template: {scene}. Camera: tilt down. Movement: rotate the camera downward from one fixed point. Speed: smooth constant tilt. Framing: keep the vertical subject or architecture centered as the frame travels downward. End: land on the lower target.
best_for: Descending a subject or revealing what lies below the eyeline.
tips: Start on the top of the subject and name the lower target the shot should land on.
Works well as a reveal: sky or ceiling first, then the subject below.

name: Slow zoom in
description: Gradual optical push toward a tighter frame.
prompt: slow zoom in. Movement: slowly increase lens focal length toward a tighter frame. Speed: gradual and even. Framing: keep the main visual target readable as it becomes larger in frame. End: finish on a stable tighter composition.
prompt_template: {scene}. Camera: slow zoom in. Movement: slowly increase lens focal length toward a tighter frame. Speed: gradual and even. Framing: keep the main visual target readable as it becomes larger in frame. End: finish on a stable tighter composition.
best_for: Building tension and drawing the eye toward an emotional beat.
tips: Center the subject in the start frame so the zoom tightens on it rather than drifting off.
Use "zoom", not "move closer"; the second phrasing invites a dolly with parallax.

name: Slow zoom out
description: Gradual optical pull toward a wider frame.
prompt: slow zoom out. Movement: slowly decrease lens focal length toward a wider frame. Speed: gradual and even. Framing: keep the main visual target readable as more surrounding space appears. End: finish on a stable wider composition.
prompt_template: {scene}. Camera: slow zoom out. Movement: slowly decrease lens focal length toward a wider frame. Speed: gradual and even. Framing: keep the main visual target readable as more surrounding space appears. End: finish on a stable wider composition.
best_for: Revealing context and letting a subject shrink into its world.
tips: Leave believable surroundings implied at the frame edges so the zoom out has a world to reveal.
Pair with a still subject; people walking out of frame fight the reveal.

name: Fast zoom in
description: Quick decisive optical push to a tighter frame.
prompt: fast zoom in. Movement: quickly increase lens focal length toward the main visual target. Speed: quick decisive zoom. Framing: keep the target centered or clearly readable during the scale change. End: finish on a stable tighter composition.
prompt_template: {scene}. Camera: fast zoom in. Movement: quickly increase lens focal length toward the main visual target. Speed: quick decisive zoom. Framing: keep the target centered or clearly readable during the scale change. End: finish on a stable tighter composition.
best_for: Punchy emphasis — snapping attention to a detail or reaction.
tips: Name the exact detail the zoom lands on (eyes, a ring, a clock face).
Keep the landing frame sharp: add "finish in focus" to the End line.

name: Fast zoom out
description: Quick decisive optical pull to a wider frame.
prompt: fast zoom out. Movement: quickly decrease lens focal length away from the main visual target. Speed: quick decisive zoom. Framing: keep the target readable as the surrounding space appears. End: finish on a stable wider composition.
prompt_template: {scene}. Camera: fast zoom out. Movement: quickly decrease lens focal length away from the main visual target. Speed: quick decisive zoom. Framing: keep the target readable as the surrounding space appears. End: finish on a stable wider composition.
best_for: Sudden context reveals and comedic or shock beats.
tips: Start tight on one detail and name the wide context the pull reveals.
Short clips hold the energy; longer ones slow down into a regular zoom out.

name: Crash zoom in
description: Violent snap zoom toward the target.
prompt: crash zoom in. Movement: snap the lens rapidly toward the main visual target. Speed: very fast and punchy. Framing: keep the target readable through the sudden scale change. End: land on a bold tighter composition.
prompt_template: {scene}. Camera: crash zoom in. Movement: snap the lens rapidly toward the main visual target. Speed: very fast and punchy. Framing: keep the target readable through the sudden scale change. End: land on a bold tighter composition.
best_for: High-impact stingers, meme energy, and aggressive emphasis.
tips: Keep the clip very short; a crash zoom is a punctuation mark, not a shot.
Place the target dead center in the start frame so the snap stays on it.

name: Crash zoom out
description: Violent snap zoom away from the target.
prompt: crash zoom out. Movement: snap the lens rapidly away from the main visual target. Speed: very fast and punchy. Framing: keep the target readable as the surrounding space appears. End: land on a bold wider composition.
prompt_template: {scene}. Camera: crash zoom out. Movement: snap the lens rapidly away from the main visual target. Speed: very fast and punchy. Framing: keep the target readable as the surrounding space appears. End: land on a bold wider composition.
best_for: Explosive reveals and hard tonal shifts.
tips: Keep the clip very short and land on a wide frame that explains the moment.
Comedic reveals work best when the wide frame adds new information.

name: Dolly in
description: Camera body physically pushes forward toward the subject.
prompt: dolly in. Movement: move the camera physically forward in a straight line toward the main subject. Speed: smooth controlled push. Framing: keep camera height, lens direction and subject position consistent while distance closes. End: finish in a tighter composition.
prompt_template: {scene}. Camera: dolly in. Movement: move the camera physically forward in a straight line toward the main subject. Speed: smooth controlled push. Framing: keep camera height, lens direction and subject position consistent while distance closes. End: finish in a tighter composition.
best_for: Intimacy with parallax — closing on a subject as the world slides past.
tips: Ask for visible parallax ("foreground passes faster than the background") so it reads as a dolly, not a zoom.
One straight push per clip; chain a second clip from the last frame to go further.

name: Dolly out
description: Camera body physically retreats from the subject.
prompt: dolly out. Movement: move the camera physically backward in a straight line away from the main subject. Speed: smooth controlled retreat. Framing: keep lens direction and camera height consistent while more environment enters frame. End: finish in a wider composition.
prompt_template: {scene}. Camera: dolly out. Movement: move the camera physically backward in a straight line away from the main subject. Speed: smooth controlled retreat. Framing: keep lens direction and camera height consistent while more environment enters frame. End: finish in a wider composition.
best_for: Endings and isolation — pulling away to leave a subject in space.
tips: Keep the subject still and centered so the retreat does the storytelling.
Great as a closing shot: end on the subject small inside the space.

name: Tracking shot
description: Camera travels through the scene with the subject.
prompt: tracking shot. Movement: move through the scene with the main subject. Speed: match the subject pace. Framing: keep the subject consistently readable while the environment moves around them. End: maintain a clear moving composition.
prompt_template: {scene}. Camera: tracking shot. Movement: move through the scene with the main subject. Speed: match the subject pace. Framing: keep the subject consistently readable while the environment moves around them. End: maintain a clear moving composition.
best_for: Sustained motion — staying with a subject as they move through a space.
tips: Give the subject a clear path (corridor, street, shoreline) the camera can follow.
State the subject's direction of travel so camera and subject agree.

name: Follow shot / over-the-shoulder
description: Camera trails behind the subject at shoulder height.
prompt: follow shot from behind. Movement: move behind the subject along their route at shoulder height. Speed: match the subject pace. Framing: keep the back, shoulder or head as the foreground guide while the route ahead stays readable. End: continue following with the subject leading the frame.
prompt_template: {scene}. Camera: follow shot from behind. Movement: move behind the subject along their route at shoulder height. Speed: match the subject pace. Framing: keep the back, shoulder or head as the foreground guide while the route ahead stays readable. End: continue following with the subject leading the frame.
best_for: Immersive journeys — putting the viewer in the subject wake.
tips: Describe what the subject is walking toward; the destination gives the shot its point.
Keep the subject's back and shoulder in frame the whole time.

name: Reverse tracking / walk-and-talk
description: Camera moves backward in front of a walking subject.
prompt: reverse tracking shot. Movement: move backward in front of the walking subject. Speed: match the subject forward pace. Framing: keep front-facing face and body framing stable as the background moves behind them. End: hold a clear front-facing moving composition.
prompt_template: {scene}. Camera: reverse tracking shot. Movement: move backward in front of the walking subject. Speed: match the subject forward pace. Framing: keep front-facing face and body framing stable as the background moves behind them. End: hold a clear front-facing moving composition.
best_for: Walk-and-talk dialogue and confident forward momentum.
tips: The subject walks toward the lens; describe their face or expression, since it is the focus.
Keep the distance constant: add "the gap between camera and subject stays the same".

name: Side tracking
description: Camera glides parallel beside the subject.
prompt: side tracking shot. Movement: move parallel beside the subject along their direction of travel. Speed: match the subject motion. Framing: keep the subject in side profile or three-quarter profile at a stable distance. End: continue the parallel movement with clear horizontal motion.
prompt_template: {scene}. Camera: side tracking shot. Movement: move parallel beside the subject along their direction of travel. Speed: match the subject motion. Framing: keep the subject in side profile or three-quarter profile at a stable distance. End: continue the parallel movement with clear horizontal motion.
best_for: Profile motion — showing pace and progress across the frame.
tips: Profile framing works best; describe the subject in side view.
Foreground elements passing between camera and subject sell the speed.

name: Low tracking
description: Ground-level travel alongside the subject.
prompt: low tracking shot. Movement: move at ground or below-waist height alongside the subject movement path. Speed: match the subject, footsteps or wheels. Framing: keep the low detail readable while the ground plane moves through frame. End: finish with the low perspective clearly maintained.
prompt_template: {scene}. Camera: low tracking shot. Movement: move at ground or below-waist height alongside the subject movement path. Speed: match the subject, footsteps or wheels. Framing: keep the low detail readable while the ground plane moves through frame. End: finish with the low perspective clearly maintained.
best_for: Kinetic energy — feet, wheels, and speed felt from the ground.
tips: Describe the ground texture (wet asphalt, grass, sand) since it fills the bottom of the frame.
Feet, paws and wheels make great subjects for this height.

name: Truck left
description: Whole camera slides left on a horizontal path.
prompt: truck left. Movement: move the camera physically to the left on a straight horizontal path. Speed: smooth constant lateral travel. Framing: keep the lens facing the same direction while the scene slides across frame. End: finish on a clean lateral composition.
prompt_template: {scene}. Camera: truck left. Movement: move the camera physically to the left on a straight horizontal path. Speed: smooth constant lateral travel. Framing: keep the lens facing the same direction while the scene slides across frame. End: finish on a clean lateral composition.
best_for: Lateral reveals across a scene without changing the lens angle.
tips: Layer the scene (foreground, midground, background) so the slide produces parallax.
Keep the camera facing the same direction; a truck is a slide, not a pan.

name: Truck right
description: Whole camera slides right on a horizontal path.
prompt: truck right. Movement: move the camera physically to the right on a straight horizontal path. Speed: smooth constant lateral travel. Framing: keep the lens facing the same direction while the scene slides across frame. End: finish on a clean lateral composition.
prompt_template: {scene}. Camera: truck right. Movement: move the camera physically to the right on a straight horizontal path. Speed: smooth constant lateral travel. Framing: keep the lens facing the same direction while the scene slides across frame. End: finish on a clean lateral composition.
best_for: Lateral reveals across a scene without changing the lens angle.
tips: Layer the scene (foreground, midground, background) so the slide produces parallax.
Keep the camera facing the same direction; a truck is a slide, not a pan.

name: Pedestal up
description: Whole camera rises straight up, lens kept level.
prompt: pedestal up. Movement: move the entire camera vertically upward in a straight line. Speed: smooth constant lift. Framing: keep the lens level and pointed in the same direction during the vertical move. End: finish with the higher framing clearly readable.
prompt_template: {scene}. Camera: pedestal up. Movement: move the entire camera vertically upward in a straight line. Speed: smooth constant lift. Framing: keep the lens level and pointed in the same direction during the vertical move. End: finish with the higher framing clearly readable.
best_for: Rising to a new eyeline while holding a level horizon.
tips: Say "the lens stays level" so the model doesn't tilt instead of rise.
Good for rising over a counter, crowd or wall to reveal what is behind it.

name: Pedestal down
description: Whole camera lowers straight down, lens kept level.
prompt: pedestal down. Movement: move the entire camera vertically downward in a straight line. Speed: smooth constant descent. Framing: keep the lens level and pointed in the same direction during the vertical move. End: finish with the lower framing clearly readable.
prompt_template: {scene}. Camera: pedestal down. Movement: move the entire camera vertically downward in a straight line. Speed: smooth constant descent. Framing: keep the lens level and pointed in the same direction during the vertical move. End: finish with the lower framing clearly readable.
best_for: Dropping to a low eyeline while holding a level horizon.
tips: Say "the lens stays level" so the model doesn't tilt instead of lower.
Lower into a subject's eyeline to make the moment feel personal.

name: Arc left
description: Shallow curved move around the subject to the left.
prompt: arc left. Movement: move on a shallow curved path around the main subject toward the left side. Speed: smooth measured curve. Framing: keep distance, height and subject readability consistent while the angle changes. End: finish from a new left-side angle.
prompt_template: {scene}. Camera: arc left. Movement: move on a shallow curved path around the main subject toward the left side. Speed: smooth measured curve. Framing: keep distance, height and subject readability consistent while the angle changes. End: finish from a new left-side angle.
best_for: Adding dimension — a gentler cousin of the full orbit.
tips: Name the arc length ("a quarter turn around the subject") so it doesn't become a full orbit.
Keep the subject centered and still; the background should do the moving.

name: Arc right
description: Shallow curved move around the subject to the right.
prompt: arc right. Movement: move on a shallow curved path around the main subject toward the right side. Speed: smooth measured curve. Framing: keep distance, height and subject readability consistent while the angle changes. End: finish from a new right-side angle.
prompt_template: {scene}. Camera: arc right. Movement: move on a shallow curved path around the main subject toward the right side. Speed: smooth measured curve. Framing: keep distance, height and subject readability consistent while the angle changes. End: finish from a new right-side angle.
best_for: Adding dimension — a gentler cousin of the full orbit.
tips: Name the arc length ("a quarter turn around the subject") so it doesn't become a full orbit.
Keep the subject centered and still; the background should do the moving.

name: Orbit clockwise
description: Full circle around the subject, clockwise.
prompt: clockwise orbit. Movement: circle clockwise around the main subject at a consistent radius. Speed: smooth controlled orbit. Framing: keep the subject centered while the background rotates around them. End: complete the intended arc or full circle with stable framing.
prompt_template: {scene}. Camera: clockwise orbit. Movement: circle clockwise around the main subject at a consistent radius. Speed: smooth controlled orbit. Framing: keep the subject centered while the background rotates around them. End: complete the intended arc or full circle with stable framing.

tips: Isolated subjects with a readable background all the way around orbit best.
If the model stops early, shorten the orbit to a half circle and chain a second clip.

name: Orbit counterclockwise
description: Full circle around the subject, counterclockwise.
prompt: counterclockwise orbit. Movement: circle counterclockwise around the main subject at a consistent radius. Speed: smooth controlled orbit. Framing: keep the subject centered while the background rotates around them. End: complete the intended arc or full circle with stable framing.
prompt_template: {scene}. Camera: counterclockwise orbit. Movement: circle counterclockwise around the main subject at a consistent radius. Speed: smooth controlled orbit. Framing: keep the subject centered while the background rotates around them. End: complete the intended arc or full circle with stable framing.
best_for: Hero reveals — a true 3D turn that shows every side of a subject.
tips: Isolated subjects with a readable background all the way around orbit best.
If the model stops early, shorten the orbit to a half circle and chain a second clip.

name: Push past / pass-by shot
description: Glide forward past a foreground object into the space beyond.
prompt: push past. Movement: move forward past a visible foreground object, edge or opening. Speed: smooth forward glide. Framing: let the foreground pass close to the lens while the space beyond becomes clearer. End: arrive inside or beyond the foreground layer.
prompt_template: {scene}. Camera: push past. Movement: move forward past a visible foreground object, edge or opening. Speed: smooth forward glide. Framing: let the foreground pass close to the lens while the space beyond becomes clearer. End: arrive inside or beyond the foreground layer.
best_for: Layered depth — using a foreground wipe to reveal a new plane.
tips: Put the foreground object (a doorframe, leaves, a shoulder) right in the start frame.
Name the space beyond the object so the shot has somewhere to land.

name: Pass-through objects
description: Move toward and continue through a surface or barrier.
prompt: pass-through movement. Movement: move forward toward a visible object, surface or barrier and continue into the space beyond. Speed: smooth centered glide. Framing: keep the opening or surface centered as the transition point. End: arrive inside the revealed space beyond.
prompt_template: {scene}. Camera: pass-through movement. Movement: move forward toward a visible object, surface or barrier and continue into the space beyond. Speed: smooth centered glide. Framing: keep the opening or surface centered as the transition point. End: arrive inside the revealed space beyond.
best_for: Impossible transitions — passing through walls, screens, or portals.
tips: Choose a surface that can plausibly be passed: a window, keyhole, screen, cloud layer.
Describe both sides; the world beyond the barrier is the payoff and the end frame.

name: Handheld shot
description: Operator-height frame with natural organic sway.
prompt: handheld shot. Movement: hold the camera at human operator height with natural body movement. Speed: responsive and organic. Framing: keep the subject readable while the frame has subtle sway and micro-adjustments. End: finish with a natural handheld composition.
prompt_template: {scene}. Camera: handheld shot. Movement: hold the camera at human operator height with natural body movement. Speed: responsive and organic. Framing: keep the subject readable while the frame has subtle sway and micro-adjustments. End: finish with a natural handheld composition.
best_for: Documentary immediacy and raw, human presence.
tips: Ask for "subtle" sway; heavy shake reads as a glitch in AI video.
Documentary and verité scenes (kitchens, streets, rooms) suit it best.

name: Chase shot
description: Fast reactive pursuit of a moving subject.
prompt: chase shot. Movement: follow a moving subject quickly along the action route. Speed: fast, reactive and physically close. Framing: keep the subject visible while allowing energetic reframing. End: stay connected to the subject in motion.
prompt_template: {scene}. Camera: chase shot. Movement: follow a moving subject quickly along the action route. Speed: fast, reactive and physically close. Framing: keep the subject visible while allowing energetic reframing. End: stay connected to the subject in motion.
best_for: Action and urgency — staying glued to a subject in flight.
tips: Give the subject and the route clear direction ("running left down the alley").
Short clips keep the action coherent; chain for longer pursuits.

name: Body-mounted camera / Snorricam
description: Camera fixed to the subject; the world moves around them.
prompt: body-mounted Snorricam. Movement: keep the camera fixed relative to the subject torso or face while the subject moves. Speed: match the subject body motion. Framing: keep the subject close, centered and facing the camera as the background moves around them. End: finish with the subject still locked in frame.
prompt_template: {scene}. Camera: body-mounted Snorricam. Movement: keep the camera fixed relative to the subject torso or face while the subject moves. Speed: match the subject body motion. Framing: keep the subject close, centered and facing the camera as the background moves around them. End: finish with the subject still locked in frame.
best_for: Disorientation and intensity — the subject still, the world reeling.
tips: Frame the subject's face or torso tight and centered; the background should swing, not the subject.
Disorientation, panic and euphoria are the natural moods for this rig.

name: Crane up
description: Smooth vertical lift through open space.
prompt: crane up. Movement: travel smoothly upward through open space. Speed: slow controlled vertical lift. Framing: keep the subject or location readable as the camera rises. End: finish with the higher scale clearly visible.
prompt_template: {scene}. Camera: crane up. Movement: travel smoothly upward through open space. Speed: slow controlled vertical lift. Framing: keep the subject or location readable as the camera rises. End: finish with the higher scale clearly visible.
best_for: Grand reveals — rising off a subject to expose the wider world.
tips: Start close to the subject and name the high final view (rooftops, crowd, valley).
Open space above the subject gives the lift room.

name: Crane down
description: Smooth vertical descent through open space.
prompt: crane down. Movement: travel smoothly downward through open space. Speed: slow controlled vertical descent. Framing: keep the subject or location readable as the camera descends. End: finish with the lower subject or destination clearly visible.
prompt_template: {scene}. Camera: crane down. Movement: travel smoothly downward through open space. Speed: slow controlled vertical descent. Framing: keep the subject or location readable as the camera descends. End: finish with the lower subject or destination clearly visible.
best_for: Descending into a scene or arriving on a subject from above.
tips: Start on a wide overhead view and name the subject the descent lands on.
Classic opening move: world first, then the character.

name: Drone push in
description: Aerial forward glide toward the subject.
prompt: drone push in. Movement: fly smoothly forward through open space toward the subject or destination. Speed: controlled aerial glide. Framing: keep the route and destination readable as the camera approaches. End: arrive at a closer aerial composition.
prompt_template: {scene}. Camera: drone push in. Movement: fly smoothly forward through open space toward the subject or destination. Speed: controlled aerial glide. Framing: keep the route and destination readable as the camera approaches. End: arrive at a closer aerial composition.
best_for: Sweeping approaches — flying in on a location or hero subject.
tips: Describe the destination (a cabin, a cliff edge, a lone figure) as the end of the flight.
Big landscapes and clear sky read best; tight interiors fight a drone move.

name: Drone pull back
description: Aerial backward glide revealing more landscape.
prompt: drone pull back. Movement: fly smoothly backward away from the subject or destination. Speed: controlled aerial retreat. Framing: keep the subject readable as more landscape appears. End: finish on a wider aerial composition.
prompt_template: {scene}. Camera: drone pull back. Movement: fly smoothly backward away from the subject or destination. Speed: controlled aerial retreat. Framing: keep the subject readable as more landscape appears. End: finish on a wider aerial composition.
best_for: Epic reveals — pulling back to show scale and isolation.
tips: Start close on the subject and name the landscape the pull reveals.
Keep the subject centered as it shrinks; it anchors the reveal.

name: Helicopter shot
description: High-altitude broad flight path over a landscape.
prompt: helicopter-style aerial shot. Movement: move from high altitude along a broad gradual flight path. Speed: steady controlled aerial motion. Framing: keep the landscape or distant moving subject readable at wide scale. End: finish on a stable high-altitude composition.
prompt_template: {scene}. Camera: helicopter-style aerial shot. Movement: move from high altitude along a broad gradual flight path. Speed: steady controlled aerial motion. Framing: keep the landscape or distant moving subject readable at wide scale. End: finish on a stable high-altitude composition.
best_for: Establishing scale — vast landscapes and sweeping geography.
tips: Describe scale and terrain (coastline, mountain ridge, city grid) rather than a small subject.
Golden hour or storm light gives aerial shots depth.

name: First-person view
description: POV from the character own eyes, with visible body.
prompt: first-person view. Movement: move forward at human eye height from the character perspective. Speed: natural walking or reaching pace. Framing: use visible hands, arms or body edges as the viewer physical reference. End: arrive at the next point of action from the same point of view.
prompt_template: {scene}. Camera: first-person view. Movement: move forward at human eye height from the character perspective. Speed: natural walking or reaching pace. Framing: use visible hands, arms or body edges as the viewer physical reference. End: arrive at the next point of action from the same point of view.
best_for: Immersion and gaming energy — putting the viewer inside the scene.
tips: Mention visible hands or arms in frame so the model commits to the POV.
Describe what the character reaches for or walks toward.

name: Tilt-shift
description: Miniature-look with a narrow band of sharp focus.
prompt: tilt-shift miniature view. Movement: hold or glide from a high angled view over the scene. Speed: small precise movement. Framing: keep a narrow band of sharp focus across the key subject area with soft blur above and below. End: finish with the miniature-scale view intact.
prompt_template: {scene}. Camera: tilt-shift miniature view. Movement: hold or glide from a high angled view over the scene. Speed: small precise movement. Framing: keep a narrow band of sharp focus across the key subject area with soft blur above and below. End: finish with the miniature-scale view intact.
best_for: Playful miniature worlds and stylized establishing shots.
tips: Use a high angle over busy scenes: streets, markets, rail yards, festivals.
Bright, saturated light strengthens the miniature illusion.
negatives: shallow focus on one subject only

name: Infinite zoom
description: Continuous accelerating zoom into the center.
prompt: infinite zoom. Movement: zoom continuously inward toward the exact center target. Speed: smooth accelerating zoom. Framing: keep the circular target centered as it expands. End: finish when the next visual world fills the frame.
prompt_template: {scene}. Camera: infinite zoom. Movement: zoom continuously inward toward the exact center target. Speed: smooth accelerating zoom. Framing: keep the circular target centered as it expands. End: finish when the next visual world fills the frame.
best_for: Dreamlike loops and seamless world-to-world transitions.
